overview: This five-page bundle consists of U.S. Department of State “List of Papers” index sheets rather than the underlying correspondence itself. The sheets catalogue reports, memoranda, letters, and cross-references concerning Japanese industrial production and trade, particularly synthetic ammonia and fertilizer, iodine, textile dyes, soda, and matches. The entries document proposed transfers of du Pont chemical processes to Mitsui, Japanese price and production policies, wartime economic intelligence, foreign-exchange restrictions, an iodine export agreement with Chile, and an investigation of the claim that Japanese matches marked “Made in Sweden” came from a Japanese locality named Sweden.

subfiles.title: General list of papers on Japanese manufactures
subfiles.about: Index to reports on Japanese ammonia, matches, chemical research, textile dyes, and soda production.
subfiles.summary: Docket covers a DuPont ammonia-process deal, a Match Company closure, dye-import barriers, and Japan's soda industry.

subfiles.title: List of papers on ammonia manufacture in Japan
subfiles.about: Index to correspondence and memoranda about du Pont’s sale of synthetic-ammonia and hydrogen-process rights to Mitsui.
subfiles.summary: Docket covers DuPont's ammonia-process sale negotiations with a Japanese firm tied to Mitsui, with State staying uninvolved.

subfiles.title: List of papers on fertilizer manufacture in Japan
subfiles.about: Index to reports on fertilizer price regulation and the relationship between Japanese fertilizer supplies and food production.
subfiles.summary: Docket covers Japanese farmer demands for fertilizer price controls, and British intelligence on wartime fertilizer policy.

subfiles.title: List of papers on iodine in Japan
subfiles.about: Index entry for a report on the 1937 Japan–Chile agreement regulating iodine exports and prices.
subfiles.summary: Docket covers a 1937 Chile-Japan iodine export-price agreement, with annual production figures for both countries.

subfiles.title: List of papers on matches and the alleged Japanese town of Sweden
subfiles.about: Index to an inquiry into the claim that a Japanese locality named Sweden produced matches labeled “Made in Sweden.”
subfiles.summary: Docket traces a debunked claim that a Japanese town called Sweden made matches labeled 'Made in Sweden.'

interest: Shows 1930s US tracking of Japanese chemical industry deals, trade barriers, and an odd matchbox-labeling rumor.
